\newcommand{\SecResearchAreas}{%
\section{Research Areas}
Measurement, reporting, and data quality; mortality measurement, validation, and health information systems; demographic inference under incomplete and misclassified data; verbal autopsy and cause-of-death surveillance; survey validation and measurement error; demographic and Bayesian estimation; computational text analysis and multimodal machine learning; research software, data infrastructure, and civil registration and vital statistics systems.
}

% Research-scientist variant only.
\newcommand{\SecSummary}{%
\section{Summary}
Interdisciplinary population health scientist and demographer working at the intersection of epidemiology and data science. Research spans reporting bias and survey validation, mortality measurement and health information systems, and demographic inference under incomplete and misclassified data. Platform manager and core developer of the WHO-hosted Reference Data Archive, co-leading software development with the Africa Health Research Institute, and developer of MultimodalVA. First- or joint-first-author population research in \emph{Lancet Global Health}; contracts with WHO and KIT Royal Tropical Institute and technical work with the Ministry of Health of Guinea-Bissau. R, Python, Julia, SQL; Bayesian, demographic, and machine-learning methods.
}

\newcommand{\SecSoftware}{%
\Needspace{15\baselineskip}
\section{Research Software, Data Products, and Infrastructure}
\cventry{2023--present}{\textbf{MultimodalVA} --- Python package for cause-of-death classification from verbal autopsy data.\newline
Role: developer and maintainer. Unified interface for narrative-only, indicator-only, and multimodal models (data fusion, feature fusion, soft voting, and stacking), with hyperparameter optimization, evaluation metrics, and visualization. The development version also includes a prompt-based language-model pipeline for open-weight chat models, including gpt-oss, through Hugging Face or local serving with Ollama. Publicly released, MIT-licensed, typed Python package. \href{https://github.com/y-chu/MultimodalVA}{GitHub}; study preprint: \url{https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.15.26364476}}
\cventry{2023--present}{\textbf{Reference Data Archive (RDA) software and data platform} --- WHO-hosted reference mortality data infrastructure. Julia, Python, R, SQL.\newline
Pilot contribution at The Ohio State University, 2023--May 2025; continued under a formal WHO contract beginning June 2025. Platform in operation and open to users. Role: platform manager and core developer; co-lead of software development with the Africa Health Research Institute; sole data manager. Wrote the data processing pipeline, the Julia user API, and RDANada.jl, which publishes DDI metadata to the NADA catalogue through its REST API (sole author; deployed in the WHO-hosted analytics environment; available on request); co-developed the ingestion package, extending its original framework and schema. Protocols, standard operating procedures and user guidance; user and data-access management. Public repositories: \href{https://github.com/RDAORG/RDAIngest.jl}{RDAIngest.jl} (data ingestion; co-lead developer) and \href{https://github.com/RDAORG/juRDA.jl}{juRDA.jl} (Julia user API; author). \url{https://data.who.int/platforms/rda}}
\cventry{2022}{\textbf{Verbal Autopsy: Reimagining Data and Automated Cause Assignment (ALPHA network data)} --- curated, anonymised verbal-autopsy, residency and HIV surveillance data for scientific use, South Africa, 2000--2020; NIH-funded; deposited in the Africa Health Research Institute data catalogue (AHRI.NIH.Verbal.Autopsy.Dataset.v1, version 1.0.0).\newline
Role: one of four named primary investigators in the catalogue record, with S. J. Clark, C. Calvert and M. Marston. Licensed access administered by DataFirst, University of Cape Town. \url{https://data.ahri.org/index.php/catalog/1030}}
}
